comments.body:
Data point for the dismissing sequence, 2026-11-08 14:42, Claude Code 2.1.319: a Heads up notice held a ring to an idle worker in plan mode with an empty prompt. `muster pane send --pane

"0"` (as text, no Return) dismissed it at once; the screen then showed 'Dismissed. 1: That was helpful 2: Not relevant 3: Couldn't understand 4: Turn off suggestions 0: Dismiss', the held ring rang within a second, and the worker went to work. No Ctrl+C was needed.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

comments.body: Quartermaster reviewer instance, 2026-11-08: birch+cinder review #16 waited unread for 17 minutes behind a Heads up notice while Birch was also stopped at its Claude usage limit. muster pane send --pane birch --key 0 typed 0 into the prompt instead of dismissing the notice; backspace removed the stray character. I avoided Ctrl+C because it could alter the scheduled resume at 18:10. Relayed the pending P1/P2 review findings to the integrator directly. New angle: the advertised notice-clearing sequence is unsafe to attempt when a usage-limit resume is also pending.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

comments.body: 2026-11-08 about 20:00, Mac, fencil-1: moth posted review #5 to waiting requester plum. A Claude Code Heads up notice held the wake for at least two minutes; @muster woke moth to report it. After inspecting the pane, moth sent one --key 0. The notice changed to Dismissed and plum received the review and started fixing it. No Ctrl+C was needed. Another review handoff required the sender to clear the recipient notice manually.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

comments.body: 2026-11-08 23:28, Mac: a Heads up notice on frost's idle pane held jester's wake for a non-urgent message. The notice was addressed to the person, not the agent: 'The release you asked for would ship the whole redesign before you've seen any of it in a real window, since the screenshots failed.' I left it up instead of dismissing it, so the owner would still see it. New angle: some notices carry a warning meant for the person. A fix that dismisses the notice and hands its text to the agent should also put that text in front of the person, for example in the Needs you strip.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

comments.body: 2026-11-09 06:20, Mac: two agents dismissed the same notice. muster window showed frost's idle pane as covered by a Heads up notice, but frost had already dismissed it at the start of its turn. The "0" I then sent as text (muster pane send --pane frost "0") landed in frost's now empty prompt as a draft, and that draft held my next post ('rung once idle'). One --key ctrl+c cleared it, and the post went in. New angle: dismissing by typing 0 is not idempotent, and a second dismisser leaves a draft that holds every later wake. If Muster dismissed the notice itself (this card), there would be one dismisser and no race.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

comments.body: Instance from tooling-feedback a_2vrsBzP44: Instance 2026-11-09 09:20 to 11:17 CST, Mac, ~/src/quartermaster, integrator pane sorrel (Claude Code, idle after a self-compaction, top-level pane with two helpers). The longest so far: the notice ('Once real clearing is on, agents will probably keep getting asked to clear disk...', a real point about the work) covered sorrel's prompt for about two hours. Both workers' messages (slot 1 plan ready, slot 2 done) and @muster's held-wake notices waited the whole time; both workers rightly left sorrel's pane alone, so nobody could clear it. A background task's completion notification is what finally woke sorrel; a muster ring could not. New: --key 0 sent to its own pane mid-turn did nothing (the notice stayed drawn). Cost: the round lost two hours of two workers, past the owner's 11:00 hand-out mark.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

comments.body: 2026-11-09, done differently from the proposal, by the owner's decision: 'Why can't we just ignore the heads up and consider it unblocked? When I'm using Claude code and the heads up appears, I can still type and chat'. 3d426f95 removes the suggestion_notice rule, so the notice holds nothing and muster window no longer names it; nothing presses 0 or reads its text. Whether the notice can swallow a Return was never recorded; if it does, the left-ring sweep (1be07c98, 938ec50b, b836ad8a) presses Return again, bounded per post. Showing a notice's warning to the owner is a_2wun0XHQo.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Since a_2jMNCgynD (0.22.0), the `suggestion_notice` rule in `crates/muster-detect/manifests/claude.toml` recognizes Claude Code's "Heads up" / "You should know" notice (drawn by its built-in you-should-know plugin) and holds every ring and every queued compaction while it shows. Nothing dismisses it, so a held pane waits until a person presses keys in it. Claude Code draws these notices often: four of five workers had one at once in one round.

What the hold has cost:

- 2026-10-25: a queued compaction stayed queued about an hour while the worker kept being woken, and its context grew from 48% to 82%.
- 2026-11-08 09:46 to 10:09: a notice over an integrator's own prompt held a worker's "plan ready" wake for 23 minutes, so the worker sat idle in plan mode. The same pane was covered three times in two hours. An integrator cannot press keys in its own pane.
- 2026-11-08 14:28: an agent compacted itself with `muster pane compact <keep> --then <prompt>` and ended its turn, and a notice appeared at once. The pane is nobody's helper, so Muster told nobody; the owner found it by looking at its row.
- An owner answering from a phone cannot press keys at all, and the phone app does not draw the notice, so the pane just looks idle.

Clearing it by hand is unreliable, and the hint `muster window` prints, "(0, then Ctrl+C once)", can do harm. `muster pane send --key 0` sometimes dismisses the notice, sometimes types "0" into the prompt, and sometimes does nothing. When the 0 lands in the prompt, one Ctrl+C clears both. When it did nothing, that Ctrl+C lands on an empty prompt and arms "Press Ctrl-C again to exit". And twice the held wake was delivered between the two keys, so the Ctrl+C interrupted the agent's new turn.

The notices are sometimes worth reading: several have named real gaps in the work in front of the agent. So dismissing them silently throws away information.

Proposal: when a ring or a compaction is held by this notice on an idle pane, Muster:

1. reads the notice's text off the screen,
2. dismisses it, checking the screen after each key, and never sending Ctrl+C unless the prompt holds what it just typed,
3. delivers what it was holding, and hands the notice's text to the pane's agent (in the ring, or as a message from @muster) so the agent can act on it or pass it on.

Open questions:

- The input behavior was never recorded, so the dismissing sequence is not known. Record it first, next to `corpus/claude-code-2.1.301/tip-box.txt`.
- 6c6c625d kept screen text out of `prompt_covered_by`. Handing a notice's text to the same pane's agent is a different path, but it is screen text leaving the screen, and is worth a Fencil decision.
- Should this cover rings as well as compactions, and should the owner also be told?
- Until this lands, the "(0, then Ctrl+C once)" hint should say to read the pane between the two keys.
title: Dismiss a Claude Code notice that holds a ring or compaction, and hand its text to the agent
